title: Narration That Survives a 4km Dead Zone | vitalii.no
description:
My delivery route runs through long stretches with no mobile signal, and the app's narration used to just die mid-sentence - or worse, keep describing a place long after I'd already driven past it, which made the whole feature feel broken rather than smart.

I added a drive-pack endpoint that bundles every nearby story and street segment into one response, so the Android app can match the car's GPS position locally without a live network call. It refreshes the pack every 10 minutes while connected, prefetches audio up to 8 km ahead into an on-device cache, and queues any offline plays to report back later. Playback itself now tracks the car's position against each story's own sentence boundaries, so if I drive past a place mid-story, the current sentence finishes and the story stops cleanly instead of overlapping whatever comes next.

A 4 km stretch with zero signal now produces continuous narration instead of silence, and stories interrupted by a drive-past resume cleanly on the next pass instead of restarting or talking over the next place. An end-to-end test suite covers both scenarios directly.
